bloques: A native PC port of a GameCube fighting game (disc ID GRSEAF), produced by static recompilation rather than emulation: the disc's PowerPC executable is translated ahead of time into C, compiled for x86-64, and run as native code inside a Dolphin-derived runtime that provides the graphics, audio, input and hardware emulation around it.
No game data and no game code are distributed here. You supply a disc image you already own; setup extracts it and recompiles it on your machine.

This is still early. Expect rough edges: the game is playable start to finish, but features arrive before their polish does, and something that worked last release can break in the next one. Polish is planned throughout rather than saved up for a 1.0 — and bug reports genuinely help, because most of what gets fixed here was found by someone hitting it.

Fully playable — boots to menu and through gameplay. Every block of the game's own executable runs as native code; the recompiler translates 535,368 instructions with 0 unknown opcodes and no interpreter fallback inside them.

What the interpreter does still cover is the PowerPC exception vectors — 0x500 (external interrupt), 0xC00 (system call), 0x800 (FP unavailable). Those handlers are written into low RAM by the OS at boot rather than living in the disc's executable, so there is no recompiled code to dispatch to and the interpreter runs them until control returns. They account for about 0.7% of executed steps, steadily, because interrupts fire for the life of the session — but only 0.2% of cycles, so there is nothing to win by recompiling them. An earlier version of this page claimed "zero interpreter…
Rendering is Vulkan on the GPU, with the CPU emulation and the runtime on separate cores.

Steam Deck: supported, with its own package, and it runs in both Desktop and Game Mode at 45–49 fps in a match. Two ways to get a module onto it, so it works whether or not the Deck is the only machine you have:

Build it on the Deck. Install a toolchain once and SteamOS compiles its own module, needing no bundled libraries at all — no second computer anywhere in the process. Tested end to end on SteamOS 3.8.25. This is also the way to get the full PGO win there, since clang 20 cannot read the shipped profiles.
Build it on a desktop and copy it over. No toolchain on the Deck at all, if you have another Linux machine to hand.

bloques: A native PC port of God of War (PS2, NTSC-U SCUS-97399) built by statically recompiling MIPS R5900 code to C++, with an installer launcher, one-click build, fan-translation support and a 60 fps target.

0.6.1 (stable): new in-game menu with pause and persistent settings, native save-slot loading, altar backups, device-aware button prompts, short and reliable keyboard stick QTEs (also automatic in Accessibility), movie flash fix and a shipped PGO profile. See what's new and the changelog.

Linux / Steam Deck (experimental): native launcher, build pipeline and Linux installer are available for testing. See installation and remaining validation. Steam Deck hardware and performance are not yet validated.

[!IMPORTANT] This repository contains no game files. You need your own legally acquired copy of God of War (the game, its disc image and any extracted assets are never distributed here). The native runtime (PS2Recomp, as extended by Waffle565, KIexster and the Tobiichi port) is required; the launcher downloads it, it is not stored here. Full attribution: CREDITS.md. These folders are created locally by the install and are not committed: data/ (prepared discs, saves, logs, recorded VU1/IOP code, portable tools), engine/runtime/ (the runtime the fetch stage clones), launcher/build*/ and…

[!WARNING] The project is not finished yet. The game is playable, but it is not 100%: a locked 60 fps is not reached in every scene, only the opening areas have been measured in depth, and some issues remain (see Known limitations). It gets better with every release, and more will be added as the community needs it — texture packs, ISO patching and experimental Linux are now available; further work is in the Roadmap. Bug reports with the launcher's session report help a lot: docs/reporting-bugs.md.

The game's executable (SCUS_973.99) is translated from MIPS to C++ by PS2Recomp and compiled into a Windows program. The runtime provides graphics, audio, input and memory-card services, with native VU1/IOP code, an in-process VU1 JIT for code not compiled yet and an interpreter as the last fallback. This project brings the work of several authors (see CREDITS.md) together behind a single installer:

Three-step installation: download the portable build tools, select your ISO and install. The runtime is downloaded automatically; a loading screen shows overall progress, estimated time remaining and tips.

One ISO is enough: the original (USA) or a recognised fan translation. With several ISOs (e.g. the original and a translation) every language becomes playable and the launcher asks which language you want to play in.

Built for speed: Windows builds use a matching profile-guided optimisation (PGO) profile. The 0.6.1 setup ships a pre-trained profile for its patch set; local training remains available. The first-play preparation records the game's VU1/IOP code in one run and builds it in as native code.
Configurable controls: full keyboard/mouse bindings, classic or modern gamepad layouts and button-by-button mapping.

Accessibility: the minigames that ask for repeated presses can be played by holding the button instead ("Hold instead of mashing" in the Accessibility tab), alongside stick gestures and texture packs.

bloques: The House of the Dead: ReWrithe
A rewrite of the arcade game and its PC port, combined.

The House of the Dead: ReWrithe is an unofficial, fan-made C++ rewrite of The House of the Dead (Sega, arcade 1996 / PC 1998). Its game logic takes the best of both versions (the PC port and the Sega Model 2C arcade game, Revision A), system by system, and it can draw the arcade version's more detailed models and textures or the PC's.

A fan-made rewrite, not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by SEGA. "The House of the Dead" is SEGA's trademark, used here only to say which game this rewrite works with. No game data is included: you need your own, legally obtained arcade ROM set and 1998 PC game (see What you need to play). Health warning (photosensitivity): the game has flashing lights (gunfire, hit flashes, the optional CRT-gun Shot Flash, which is off unless you pick the CRT Gun type). A few people may have seizures from flashing lights; stop playing if you feel unwell. Mature content: an unrated fan project with…

Expect bugs: v1.0.0 is the first public release. Every chapter plays from start to end, but not every mode, chapter and setting has been played through by a person. If something looks or plays wrong, please report it on this repository's Issues page (or tell the author directly), with settings\hotd.log and a short note of what you did. Every report helps make it match the originals.
Download the release zip (hotd-rewrithe-v1.2.0-win64.zip, GitHub Releases) and unzip it anywhere.
Double-click HOTDReWritheSetup.bat. The setup window opens:
Install to: the folder for the game (default C:\Games\HOTD ReWrithe; anywhere you like, but not Program Files).

Game files: drop your Arcade ROMs (MAME's hotd set, Revision A only) and your 1998 PC game on the two boxes, as a zip, a folder or a CD image (.iso, .bin / .cue), or click a box to choose. Each is checked at once: green is good, yellow is accepted with a note, red says why not ("This is the Saturn version", "This is the PC demo", "SOUND\GAMESNDS.RBH is missing" ...).
Options: Desktop shortcut, Start menu entry (both on), Create a VR shortcut (off; How to play in VR), Add to Steam, import the CD music (TrackNN.ogg).

Install: copies the game and only the files it needs (the 29 ROM files, the PC game's files, the music) into the folder, so your originals are not needed any more. Or Play from here without installing.
Play. From then on start the game with its shortcut; it opens at the main menu.
Uninstall: Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps > The House of the Dead: ReWrithe (no administrator needed). It asks before deleting your settings and high scores.
Change the game files later: Options > System > Repair / Change Files. What changed in a version: Options > System > What's New (also shown once after an update).
Something missing? The Game files page says what and why; details in settings\hotd.log (a crash also leaves settings\crash- .txt: attach both to a bug report, never game files).

Portable use still works: put the ROM zip in data\arcade, the PC game in data\pc and the music in data\music of the unzipped folder, and start bin\hotd.exe: with the files found it goes straight to the menu. (HOTDReWritheSetup.bat always opens the setup.) An unpatched 1998 PC copy is recommended; a patched THOTD.EXE or PC files of another version (the Japanese release, repacks) are accepted with a note. The mouse is the gun (left shoot, right reload).

A native LÖVE2D recreation of Poke Gold, Silver and Crystal, built on Gen1Recomp's Red/Blue/Yellow engine. The engine, script VM, and map behavior are hand-written Lua; game data and graphics are decoded from a ROM supplied by the player.

gen2recomp keeps everything the upstream project does for Generation I and adds the Generation II half: the Gen2 script VM and its command table, the Johto and Kanto world, day/night, breeding and the Day-Care, the Pokegear, shinies, held items, and the Gold/Silver title sequence.

It has since grown well past Generation II. The same launcher now imports and runs FireRed and Emerald (Gen 3), Platinum, HeartGold and SoulSilver (Gen 4), and Black and White (Gen 5), plus the Polished Crystal and Prism romhacks — all side by side, all from your own cartridge dumps. Around the games sit the Monster Walker (a next-gen Pokéwalker with minigames and a Watt Shop), a Map Editor, a Save Editor, machine translation into 25 languages, cloud saves, dual-screen support for the DS games, and touch controls. See What's New for the tour.

[!CAUTION] Neither this project nor Gen1Recomp is affiliated with the website gen1recomp[.]com. That site is not run by either project and was not authorized by anyone involved. Do not download anything from it, and treat anything it hosts or claims as untrustworthy. Even if it links back to a real repository, the people behind it can change its content at any time. This GitHub repository is the only official source for gen2recomp.

This project does not include a ROM, emulate the Game Boy, GBA or DS, transpile assembly, or download a disassembly. A canonical cartridge dump of one of the supported games is the only game content input.

The ROM is verified, used during import, and then released from memory. It is not copied into the cache. Later launches load the private generated cache and do not ask for the ROM again. Every version can be imported and played side by side.

Open the desktop app. On first boot, choose your legally obtained .gb / .gbc / .gba / .nds file or drop it onto the window. Import takes a few seconds for Gen 1, a couple of minutes for Gen 2, and longer for the GBA and DS games, then the game starts automatically. Have a whole folder of dumps? Tools → Import ROMs takes several files at once and imports every one it recognises.
On a console or handheld there is no file picker to open: you copy the dump into a folder the launcher scans instead. See Downloads for the exact path per device.

Only specific canonical dumps are accepted. The importer verifies SHA-1 before creating any game data; a dump it does not accept is named (game, region, revision) so you know why — see docs/rom-revisions.md.

HeartGold, SoulSilver, Black and White dumps that have had their trailing FF padding trimmed are also accepted, as long as every game byte is intact — see docs/hgss-bw-import.md. The launcher shows each game's stage on its card; Alpha and Pre-alpha games are playable but expect gaps and bugs.

The packaged app contains neither a ROM nor pre-extracted game data. Music, sound effects, and cries are synthesized while the game runs from compact audio channel programs copied out of the verified ROM.

God of War (PlayStation 2, NTSC-U SCUS-97399) statically recompiled into native C++, for Windows and, experimentally, Linux.

[!TIP] Download: the program is on the Releases page. Get the latest release: on Windows the installer (..._x64-setup.exe) or the portable zip, on Linux the .deb or the AppImage. The green Code button (and "Source code" in a release) only gives you the sources, with no installer: that is for building it yourself. You also need your own copy of the game, see Installing.

[!IMPORTANT] This is not an emulator. It is a static recompilation (recomp): the game's MIPS executable is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a native program. There is no MIPS interpreter, no emulated PS2 hardware and no BIOS at run time. docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md shows where that line falls.

[!IMPORTANT] This repository ships no game data. No ISO, no SCUS_973.99, no IRX modules, no .PAK files and no code generated from them. You need your own legal copy of the USA release of God of War for the PlayStation 2 (SCUS-97399). The installer builds everything on your machine from your own disc, and nothing derived from the game ever leaves it.

Static recompilation, not emulation. A recompiler written in Rust translates the game's MIPS code to C++, which is then compiled into a normal PC program. The PlayStation 2 hardware around it (graphics synthesizer, vector unit, I/O processor, sound, pad, memory card) is implemented natively. Nothing interprets the game's code at run time.

On top of that you get the original 60 Hz game logic (or a 120 FPS limit, the highest, at the same speed), an OpenGL renderer with 1×–8× internal resolution, native movies with sound, a launcher with settings, keyboard and mouse support, a cheat menu, target lock, widescreen, custom texture packs and RetroAchievements.

What that means in practice: the game's own code and the hardware around it are compiled C++, not something replayed. There are no emulation accuracy hacks here (frame hacks, cycle hacks, per-game patches). The port runs the game's own recompiled code and replaces the libraries that code calls with native ones.

Native renderer: OpenGL 4.6, GPU render targets, internal resolution 0.25×–8× (below 1× for integrated GPUs), bicubic (with sharpening), bilinear or pixel upscaling, FXAA, 480p progressive mode, brightness/contrast/gamma/saturation adjustment.
Widescreen (Hor+): 16:9, 16:10, 21:9 (experimental) and 32:9 (very experimental: stretched HUD and menus) using PCSX2's patch. Switch it off for the game's original 4:3.
Movies: MPEG-2 decoded natively, with sound, including the game's own widescreen versions.
Controls: remappable keyboard and mouse, any gamepad, PS2 or modern layout, per-button swaps, vibration on Windows and Linux.
Quality of life: cheat menu (F2, nine cheats), target lock (Alt), agile combat, overlay with FPS, GPU, CPU and RAM (each one optional), fullscreen.

Saves: a PCSX2-compatible Mcd001.ps2 memory card. Cards move between the two in either direction. A dated copy of the card is kept at every altar save. The launcher's Saves tab shows each save with its altar, thumbnail, difficulty and play time, loads one even with the game open, and restores a copy.
Custom textures: PCSX2 replacement packs work, and the launcher can download the community pack.
Steam and shortcuts: the launcher can open the game directly, without its window, and close with it, so it can be added to Steam as a non-Steam game (docs/LAUNCHER.md).
RetroAchievements: sign-in, in-game notifications and a hardcore mode that disables cheats.
Launcher: nine tabs, a setup wizard, background optimization, English and Brazilian Portuguese.

bloques: Open Nectar — Pikmin and Pikmin 2 Native PC/Android Ports

Native, open-source ports of Pikmin (GameCube, 2001) and Pikmin 2 (GameCube, 2004) for Linux, Windows and Android, and macOS from source. They run the games' code directly on the host system and translate GX to OpenGL; no Dolphin or any other emulator is involved. One launcher and one Android APK carry both games.
This project builds upon the decompilations by projectPiki/pikmin and projectPiki/pikmin2 and adds a native port layer.
This project was developed with the assistance of AI tools. The generated code was reviewed, tested and integrated by me. I mention it because I'd rather be upfront about how this was built.

To make it clear: I'm a coder and I use claude as a tool not as a substitute. I know what is done in my project and how it is done, main problem with open nectar is that I don't have testers, I test myself on my devices where it works fine and once released I fix all the issues reported. Please consider to try the latest release
Playable from start to finish, natively, on Linux, Windows and Android, from the USA (GPVE01) and European (GPVP01) discs:
30, 60 and 120 FPS, or your monitor's refresh rate: gameplay keeps the original timing while animations and cutscenes are interpolated
The original audio engine, with the console's DSP levels
Console-accurate details: see-through helmet glass with reflections and indirect texture effects (heat haze, geysers, cave holes)
F1 settings menu drawn with Pikmin 2's own assets
Randomizer, Speedrun mode with timer and splits, Hard and Permadeath rules, and a captain selector
Optional mods shared with Pikmin 1: swarm at the cursor, Better Pathfinding, Blues Only In Water, Lock-On and Charge, Eternal Night
Texture packs, with a one-click HD pack download in the launcher
Touch controls, touch menus and button icons on Android
Native builds for Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64, Android from the same source
Most of the game playable from start to finish
Full audio: the game's original JAudio engine, with a software DSP
Controller, keyboard and mouse support, touch controls

Both retail discs: Pikmin USA Rev 1 and Pikmin Europe. The European disc carries five languages — English, French, German, Spanish and Italian — switchable from the launcher, F1 or the game's own options
Pre-rendered movies: the attract movies play, with sound
Widescreen: the HUD is laid out for 16:9 rather than stretched, and the 3D view culls to the same shape, so nothing pops in and out at the sides
Post-processing: antialiasing, restored fog, bloom, ambient occlusion, depth of field, texture filtering and colour grading — every one of them optional
Custom texture packs, with a one-click HD pack download in the launcher
Randomizer: ship parts, enemies and bosses, with share codes
Nectar Map Maker: an editor for VS arenas, opened from the launcher
Local co-op: Olimar and Louie, two controllers, split screen that can merge into a single camera; Louie also playable in single player
HD character models from Pikmin 3 rips
Per-pixel lighting and real-time shadow maps (Off/Soft/Normal/Strong), both optional
Launcher: installs, updates itself from GitHub releases, and exposes every F1 setting, texture packs and HD models outside the game
Speedrun mode: pure GameCube rules, a real-time timer, per-day splits against your best run, categories, LiveSplit support and an input display
Skippable cutscenes: Start skips any cutscene in normal play
Grab the package for your system from Releases.

bloques: An unofficial PC port of Ratchet & Clank (PlayStation 2, 2002), written in Rust. It runs the full game, start to credits, from your own disc.

No game data is included. This repository contains no game code, graphics, sound, text or other game files. The setup reads your own copy of the disc and creates everything it needs on your PC. You need to own the game.

Project site: https://asobicodes.dev Launcher (optional app to play, update, and manage texture packs and mods): https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs-launcher Support the project (no pressure tho!): https://ko-fi.com/asobicodes
The whole game is playable from power-on to the end credits, including New Game+.

Gameplay follows the original PS2 game one to one. On top of that, the PC version has widescreen, keyboard and mouse controls, gamepad support, and an optional modern camera (mouse look and strafing).

Optional modern graphics on the Graphics page (Pause > Options > Graphics): enhanced lighting with volumetric fog, 3D clouds and shining stars, global illumination, ambient occlusion, dynamic shadows, clear reflective water with waves and tides, vegetation, animated fire that lights the scene, rising volumetric smoke, fur on Ratchet, shiny metal, sun rays, frame smoothing and a sharp HUD, each with quality levels, plus a Graphics Preset row (Low / Medium / High / Custom). The Classic settings keep the original PS2 look.
Two renderers: Vulkan (the default) and DirectX 12 (Options > Graphics > Screen > Renderer). ReShade works with both.
Upscalers (since v0.5, Windows): AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) and, on NVIDIA RTX graphics cards, NVIDIA DLSS (Graphics > Resolution > Upscaler), with Vulkan and DirectX 12. See Upscalers.

Modern menus (since v0.5): the title screen, pause menu, vendor, Galactic Map, Save / Load, Quick Select, Controls and Mods as modern pages with mouse support. The Classic menus stay (Graphics > Menu style).
Achievements (since v0.5): 35 achievements, shown as toasts when you earn them, in the pause menu's Achievements tab and in the launcher.
Aspect ratio (since v0.5): Auto, 4:3, 16:9, 16:10, 21:9 or 32:9 (Display > Screen > Aspect ratio).
RAC-RS Launcher (since v0.4): a separate app to play, change every option, manage texture packs and mods, keep several game versions side by side, and update with a backup first. See Launcher.
Mods (since v0.4): script mods through the bundled OmniLoader mod loader. Arsenal Mastery comes preinstalled and switched off. See Mods and texture packs.
PCSX2 texture packs (since v0.4): packs made for PCSX2 work as they are.
Plays from the PAL / Europe disc and, since v0.2, from the USA disc.
Windows 10 and 11, and since v0.4.1 Linux (x86-64). See Linux.
Known issues are listed under Known issues below.

The game runs on its own original code. When you run setup, it translates the PS2 code from your disc into native Rust ("static recompilation"), and that code runs on a PS2 CPU core written in Rust. Because the game logic is the original code, gameplay behaves exactly like the PS2 version.

Everything around the game code is native PC code written for this port: graphics, sound, movies, input, saving, and the PC features. Where a fix, a PC feature or speed needs it, an original function is rewritten in readable Rust. Changes are tested against the original: test runs play the same frames on both versions and compare the game's memory.

A faithful, fully playable PC version of Ratchet & Clank that you build from your own disc, with PC improvements on top. The game logic stays the original code. Rewriting the whole game from scratch is not a goal of this project.

The pinned shared framework uses cached HLE frame composition by default on Windows x64. Guest CPU, mapper, audio and status behavior keep their existing interfaces; this is a host presentation optimization. For the maintained correctness-reference compositor, configure a separate Release build with cmake -S . -B build-frame-lle -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSNESRECOMP_FRAME_IMPL=LLE, then cmake --build build-frame-lle. Selection is fixed at build time. LLE can reduce performance; it remains available for correctness checks. Other platforms keep LLE defaults, and existing CMake cache…

The reviewed native-view, uncapped Windows route measured 340.936 to 889.911 FPS (+161.02%, process CPU -67.17%); it includes boot/menu work and active gameplay. The owner accepted the normal-paced adaptive HLE build. These figures describe that measured build/route, not a new measurement of subsequent upstream title changes or other platforms. Foreign compiler activity limits precision. Normal play retains normal pacing/audio. See the shared framework's frame model for the host/guest boundary.

Play Mega Man X on PC with playable Zero, couch co-op and online netplay, all sixteen X2/X3 boss weapons, and adaptive widescreen. Choose Zero's original X3 combat, the optional Modern style with direct saber attacks, a second jump, and an air dash, or Saber Zero by RaphaelAzev.

A native Android APK is available alongside the desktop release, with the classic X campaign, optional Boss Rush, touch controls and Fit to screen by default. Import your own unmodified Mega Man X (USA) (Rev 1) ROM. See Android downloads and setup for platform scope and build details. The desktop release continues to provide the full mod catalog and online play.

Saber Zero is contributed by RaphaelAzev, from the MegaManXSNESRecompSaberZero fork. It gives Zero a Y-button Z-Saber: a 3-hit ground combo, air, wall and dash slashes, the X3 finisher with its Saber wave, hit-priority follow-ups, and Ride Armor pilot art. The X button keeps Zero's buster and special weapons.

To play it, choose Zero behavior → Saber Zero in either Characters → Add Zero (single player, Select switches X/Zero) or Characters → Co-op (whichever player is Zero). Both use your Mega Man X3 USA ROM, like the other Zero modes. The optional Characters → Saber Zero settings entry tunes its damage, hit priorities, finisher window and swing volume, and can outline hitboxes. Without it, Saber Zero uses RaphaelAzev's defaults.

The Saber sprites and sound effects come from the Zashiko Mod. They are included with permission under PolyForm Noncommercial with the additional permissions in PERMISSIONS.md. Controls, timings, the priority ladder and every option are in the Saber Zero reference.
Click the thumbnail to watch the gameplay showcase on YouTube.
X / Zero co-op Fight through X1 together, locally or over netplay.
Modern Zero Direct saber attacks with movement during airborne swings.
X2 / X3 weapon pages Sixteen imported boss weapons and their charged attacks.
Imported weapons in action X3's Triad Thunder on X1's Highway.
Gameplay screenshots from the project preview, plus a Modern Zero capture from the current playtest.
Checked boxes indicate available features. Configure optional mods in the launcher's Mods screen; these character and weapon mods target the USA Rev 1 build.
See the co-op validation notes for current limits.
Download the latest Windows ZIP or Linux AppImage. Extract the ZIP on Windows, or make the AppImage executable on Linux.
Open the launcher and select your own Mega Man X (USA) (Rev 1) ROM (.sfc or .smc). Headered and unheadered ROMs are supported.
Configure your keyboard or controller in Controls.
Weltall is a native port of Xenogears (PlayStation, 1998), rebuilt in Unreal Engine 5. The goal is to make the game feel like a modern PC release while keeping the original gameplay intact.

You'll need your own copy of the USA release or a supported English undub. Weltall doesn't include any game data. Put your disc images in the Games folder and the game will find them automatically. Raw images (BIN/CUE, raw IMG and CHD made from them) preserve movie audio. Images containing only 2048-byte data sectors, such as ISO, also work, but their movies are silent. Convert PBP, ECM or other formats to BIN/CUE first. You can add Disc 2 while the game is running when it asks for it. You can also start with only Disc 2, as on the PlayStation, to load your Disc 2 saves.

The undub plays with English text and Japanese voices, and its subtitles appear in the movies. If you have both versions, choose which voices you hear under Options → Sound → Voices. Options → Sound → Subtitles can also show the subtitles with the English voices, or turn them off. If you have Perfect Works Build too, Subtitles from picks the undub's subtitles or the mod's. The Sound page shows what it found, and says what you need for anything that's missing. Japanese retail discs aren't playable, but you can dump their files (see the modding guide).

Fan translations that only change the game's text, pictures and movies also play, such as the Spanish translation by Romhack Hispano. So do the French translation by Atelier Traduction (version 1.1), with English or Japanese voices, and the Italian translation by SadNES cITy (version 1.2.1), with its subtitled movies. Patch your USA discs and put the patched images in Games. If the originals are there too, the patched ones play. Weltall's own screens, such as Options, stay in English.

Status: Both discs are playable, including field exploration, character and Gear battles, the world map, menus, the Battling arena and movies. Gameplay behavior has been checked against the original game's code. I've finished my own playthrough, including the ending and a clear save. Automated tests have run every map and story battle, along with long stretches of the story from save to save. You can play from start to finish, and I'm fixing reported issues as they come in. See Reporting a problem for where to find logs and crash reports.

Higher resolutions and widescreen up to 32:9, with scenery extending beyond the original 4:3 view. On a 4:3 display, choose Options → Display → Aspect ratio → 4:3 and turn off Integer scaling to fill the screen.

Field compass placement under Options → Display. Choose 4:3, 16:9, 21:9, Screen or Off. The default is 16:9. A choice wider than the game picture uses its edge. With touch controls visible, the compass uses its original placement.
Smooth motion at any refresh rate, including 120 Hz and above, without changing the game's pace.
A free camera on the field and world map, with rotation, tilt and zoom using a mouse or right stick.
Per-pixel depth sorting to fix characters, Gears and scenery clipping or flickering over each other.
Graphics options for sharper or smoother scenery and sprites, anti-aliasing, upscaled movies, a CRT filter and integer scaling.
Softer battle flashes, or none at all, for the bright screen flashes from attacks and Ether.
Separate volumes for the music, sound effects, battle voices and movies, plus a master volume.
3D Gears on the field and world map, using their battle models, plus full-size party sprites in Gear areas.
Battle speeds of 2x and 4x, and faster text up to instant. Story battles start at normal speed. Press R1 (Camera right) to speed them up. Timed dialogue still leaves you time to read it.

A native C++ port with Arcade and Simulation, cockpit driving, desktop and VR support. The browser compiles the same game code to WebAssembly and renders with WebGL2. Gameplay fixes belong to the shared C++ code and reach each platform when it is rebuilt.
Play the browser version — select your own BIN disc image to start.

Download the file for your platform from the latest release. Each packaged build contains the game, disc importer and media tools; no compiler, SDK or toolchain is needed. The tagged source archive on GitHub still contains the full source and platform scripts for builders.

The portable GT2- -windows-x64.zip is an alternative to the MSI, and INSTALL-STEAMDECK.sh adds the Steam Deck desktop shortcut. Source kits build with INSTALL.bat, INSTALL-MACOS.command or INSTALL-STEAMDECK.sh and are only needed for development or unsupported architectures.

The Windows MSI and portable ZIP use precompiled tools; the macOS DMG and Linux Flatpak are precompiled packages. Source kits build with INSTALL.bat, INSTALL-MACOS.command or INSTALL-STEAMDECK.sh and are only needed for development or unsupported architectures. Native applications retain their platform-specific VR, controller and graphics features; the browser runs in flat-screen mode.

Supply your own supported disc images. Game data, BIOS and saves are not included. The screenshots illustrate gameplay. Release history is in CHANGELOG.md; the feature list below describes the current project.

Open the custom GT2 settings menu (F10 on desktop, the settings/menu button in VR) and read the version in its title, for example v0.9.2. Include that version, your platform and the steps to reproduce when reporting a bug. Older builds without a version label should be updated before comparing results.
Version 0.9.2 focuses on ready-to-install packages, car lights, cockpit/HUD layering and combined-disc fixes. See the changelog.

These features are still in development and are not included in 0.9.2. The existing local split-screen mode, GT4 model import and current cockpit rendering are separate features and remain available. No release dates are promised.

A fitted cockpit for live single-player Driver view, with moving steering wheel and hands, speed/RPM needles, seat adjustments and a central rear-view mirror. Replays and split-screen retain their existing views. See cockpit controls.

Native PC/Quest startup and a saved disc preference. Arcade and Simulation share graphics, HUD and control preferences while keeping separate memory cards. Desktop settings include HD media, intro visibility, all HUD switches, a profiler, gamepad bindings, keyboard bindings, DualSense pedals and both Arcade/Simulation cheats. Keyboard bindings keep Escape, Enter, Backspace, F5, F8, F10 and G reserved for existing menu/save/reset/ghost commands; rejected assignments leave the previous binding intact.
Windows PCVR through OpenXR, with theatre menus/movies, stereo races, tracked head movement and Touch controls. See PCVR setup.
USB save transfer in both directions between PC and Quest, with card validation, backups and verified copying. Desktop and PCVR share PC saves. See save transfer.

Arcade and Simulation discs, with a startup disc picker on PC and Quest, shared preferences and separate saves for each mode. Silent's combined disc installs once and appears as both modes in the picker; the browser's mode selection works with it too.
Arcade races, rally/time trials, opponent AI, ghost/replay sessions; Simulation career, licences, dealerships, garage, tuning and events.
Experimental Windows port of Resident Evil 3: Nemesis (PS1, SLUS-00923), built on the PSXRecomp static recompilation framework.
Status: work in progress / experimental. Expect bugs. Earlier release notes and this README overstated what works; this version describes the project as it actually is.
Measured, not assumed: each run writes how much code was interpreted to psx_last_run_report.json (interp_hist).
With the v1.6.1 cache, about 20 minutes of play across four sessions (new game, the RPD, doors, stairs, combat, inventory, item box, saving) peaked at 0.03%–0.15% of the emulated CPU's work.
With the disc-built cache, a session in the RPD with zombies and doors measured 0.0061%, and 17 instructions in the enemy code. What remains is BIOS code in RAM.

Earlier releases (up to v1.6.0) shipped without the overlay cache and toolchain, so the room code ran interpreted on players' machines. v1.6.1 fixed that with a cache from the maintainer's play sessions. v1.7.0 replaces it with one built from the disc.

This is not a decompilation: the game code is machine-translated, not rewritten, and the hardware is emulated. The GTE's fixed-point math is reproduced faithfully, so the PS1's polygon wobble is there underneath; the PGXP geometry correction (on by default since v2.2.2) draws the models from exact values on top of it, without changing the game's own calculations.

The release executable and the overlay shards in cache/ contain the game's machine code translated to x86-64. You must own Resident Evil 3: Nemesis (SLUS-00923) and supply your own disc image. No disc images, audio, video, textures or Sony BIOS are distributed. This is a non-commercial fan project; PSXRecomp is licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Resident Evil and related names are trademarks of Capcom; PlayStation is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment.
Status key: Works = confirmed working · Needs testing = implemented, not yet re-verified after recent changes · Known issues = reported broken or partial.

Old DirectInput-only controllers: enable "Old generic controllers (DirectInput)" in the launcher. It is off by default because on some PCs it delays startup by several seconds; Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and most other pads work without it.
Bug reports are welcome. Please include psx_last_run_report.json from the game folder and the steps to reproduce.
Download the latest zip from Releases and extract it.
Click Install Game... and select your RE3 USA disc image (.cue/.bin, raw 2352-byte sectors). 2048-byte .iso files are rejected: they lack the game's audio and video.
Pick your settings (they save on their own; technical ones are under Advanced options...), then click PLAY.

Gamepad: Left stick / D-Pad = movement (tank by default; screen-relative stick in modern mode) · A = action · X = run · Y = inventory · LB/RB = aim/fire · Back = map · Start = pause Keyboard: Arrows = move · X = action · Z = run · A = inventory · Enter = start · Alt+Enter or Ctrl+F = fullscreen · F6/F7/F8 = cheats
Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, Clang (or MinGW-w64 GCC 12+), CMake 3.20+, Ninja, Python 3.11+, and your own disc image (.cue + .bin).
Applies patches/runtime/*.patch (the RE3 changes, in order) on top of the pinned PSXRecomp commit.
-Regen recompiles the game's C from your disc into generated/. Game code is never in this repository.
Applies the two patches/re3_door_*.patch to the generated C.

bloques: Strikers - A native multi-platform port of Super Mario Strikers
Requires game data from your own copy of Super Mario Strikers. No game assets are included.

Super Mario Strikers, rebuilt to run natively on Windows, Linux, macOS and Nintendo Switch, with modern display support, online multiplayer and a focus on performance across both powerful and low-power hardware.
Built on the community decompilation by the excellent Yannick Suter, this project brings the original game to modern systems while preserving the original gameplay and visual style.
High framerate support with configurable frame limits and VSync.

Online play on a local network or over the internet, with rollback netcode (guide). The host's router opens the room's port if it supports UPnP, and friends can join from the host's Discord profile. Where the port can't be opened, Tailscale or ZeroTier are good to still reach the room.
Widescreen and ultrawide support, with an expanded view of the pitch and corrected aspect ratios.
Higher-resolution rendering with adjustable internal resolution, 4x MSAA and up to 16x anisotropic filtering.
Modern graphics backends through Metal, Vulkan and Direct3D 12 via Aurora, with experimental OpenGL and OpenGL ES options on Linux. Vulkan is personally recommended on non-macOS systems.
Controller support for Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and compatible GameCube adapters through SDL.
Button prompts follow the active keyboard or controller and its bindings with selectable controller artwork.
Customisable controls, including keyboard and gamepad bindings, stick deadzones and rumble.
Faster loading compared with original hardware.
Direct disc-image loading from ISO/GCM, CISO and GCZ files, alongside extracted game folders.
US, European and Japanese game support in one executable, with region-aware saves and language handling. The Japanese disc supports Japanese, English, German, French, Spanish and Italian.
A dedicated settings app for configuring graphics, controls, audio and game-data location. Some basic localisation included to help.
Discord Rich Presence, on by default.
Download your platform's archive above or from Releases, then follow its page on the wiki:
Linux, as an archive or an AppImage
The wiki also lists the supported discs and how to report a problem. Troubleshooting covers issues you may have playing or installing the game.
The roadmap board lists planned features and how far along each one is.
Development on the wiki covers building, running from a checkout and debugging:

This has been a solo effort. I am releasing this on what is effectively a 'burner' GitHub account because I don't want it attached to my name for professional and legal reasons. I have not done this port for reasons of ego or notoriety. Mario Strikers is one of my favourite games and it's been a dream of mine to bring it to the PC platform without the pains of emulation. My goal is simply to have it running on Steam Deck or similar low-end hardware with as little power draw as possible and nice performance, as I play the original game on Steam Deck a lot and bring it to parties and such.

Yannick Suter, who headed the decomp effort, and the other contributors deserve a ton of credit for the work that's gone into the mind-numbing process of decompilation. And of course, the team behind Aurora, for making this kind of project as easy as possible, deserve endless respect.
Thanks also to devkitPro and switchbrew for the Switch toolchain and libnx, danfromtico for NVK on Switch, and Dolphin for the texture pack format.
This project contains material with different licences and rights statuses.
Join our Discord · Open the Mod Library · Downloads

I've spent quite a bit of time working through DKR-R Online since v1.0.14. This update improves late-input recovery, reduces some of the rollback CPU work and gives spectators buffered confirmed playback. Hosts can now change the prediction window and input delay from the lobby or in-game overlay too.

There's also automatic cleanup for old downloads and caches, a tidier Play page with Start Game always within reach, and custom character names that fit Player Select. File dialogs run in a separate helper, and crash reports keep more useful diagnostic information. The unresolved startup/gameplay crashes are recorded in the crash reporting guide.
Your saves, mods and settings can stay. Use matching complete v1.0.15 packages on every machine in an online lobby. See the full release notes and changelog for everything since v1.0.14.

Online waits are reduced, not eliminated. Very slow connections can still run out of prediction history. The reported missing vanilla online car textures and other racers' road wheels remain under investigation. Physical Steam Deck Wi-Fi and separate-machine acceptance remain necessary; see validation.
DKR-R is a native static recompilation of Diddy Kong Racing. Bring your own legally obtained US v1.0 or US Rev A/v1.1 ROM. No ROM or extracted game assets are supplied.
Download the complete package for your platform from GitHub Releases.
Windows: extract the whole ZIP and start DKR-R.exe. Keep assets, libexec, helpers and licence notices together.
Linux / Steam Deck: make the AppImage executable and launch it.
Add your original ROM in Play, choose your controls and start.

The release targets Windows x64, Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64 and Steam Deck. Steam Deck uses the same payload as the Linux x86_64 AppImage. Android is not supported for current releases; macOS and iOS downloads remain on their earlier versions. See platform support and the validation record for requirements and actual coverage.

Some legacy .xdelta mods require a clean US v1.0 ROM to install, including manual imports. Add it once in Play; you can keep v1.1 selected for playing. There is no bundled revision-conversion data. See ROM setup.

Escape, F1 or controller Back/View opens the overlay. It uses the same pages as the launcher. Play contains Achievements, Session mods and Save Manager. Turn Session mods OFF for your next vanilla session without changing any individual mod selections. Ordinary offline mods still share your personal Adventure; online and development saves keep separate owners.

Start Game stays in a compact bar at the bottom while the page scrolls above it. It starts selected when a ROM is ready, and you can move away with the controller normally. The overlay uses the same position for Return to the Race.

Skip launcher boots the selected game automatically and can be turned off again in the overlay. Language changes the launcher and overlay immediately; it does not translate the ROM or community content. The initial eleven language packs are drafts awaiting native-speaker review. Seasonal colours, decorations and button patterns follow your computer's region and local date.
The left stick moves between page elements and the right stick scrolls. The sidebar switch chooses LB/RB or D-pad navigation. See the launcher guide, languages and seasonal themes.

bloques: F-ZERO GLINUX Choose your machine. Set your resolution. Hit the track. F-ZERO GX on Linux and Windows, with a controller-friendly launcher.
AppImage, Flatpak & Windows · Start playing · Unlockables · Mods · Play online · Build from source · Project status

F-ZERO GLINUX brings together a custom launcher, graphics settings and modern controller options around a Dolphin-derived runtime. Static recompilation with JIT through ModernGekko remains experimental; these packages are not a completed static recompilation release.

Bring your own F-ZERO GX USA (GFZE01) or PAL (GFZP01) image in ISO or RVZ format. Game disc contents and personal memory-card saves are not included in the packages. WIP, Issues may occur, blame the robots... but if it works its all thanks to me.
USA (GFZE01) & PAL (GFZP01) support: import either region's ISO or RVZ; PAL boots with 60Hz (EuRGB60) enabled for full 60 FPS gameplay.
Controller-friendly launcher with racing artwork, gamepad navigation and clear loading feedback.
Nine resolution presets: 480p, Steam Deck-sized 800p, 720p, 1080p, 1080p Ultrawide (2560×1080), 1440p, 1440p Ultrawide (3440×1440), 4K and 4K Ultrawide (5120×2160).
Graphics options: VSync, FXAA or 4× MSAA, texture filtering and fullscreen.
Boost on X: optional X/Y swap for modern four-button gamepads.
Z button Detect: for adapters such as the 8BitDo GBros, where Z does nothing or a full R press fires the spin attack. Click Detect under Controller and press Z on your pad.

Steering wheels (experimental, untested): an opt-in Controller setting lists your wheel, detects its steering, gas and brake axes, and uses Dolphin's GameCube steering wheel mode with force feedback in local play. Wheel drivers come from your system.

Native widescreen: use GX's own Screen Mode setting for 16:9. A 21:9 display option and three ultrawide output presets fill ultrawide monitors. The experimental local code "21:9 Ultrawide 3D & HUD" widens the 3D view and fixes the stretched HUD: tested in-game on PAL (GFZP01), briefly checked on NTSC-U (GFZE01).
Exit confirmation: Escape opens a prompt; D-pad selects, A confirms and B resumes.
Separate user data: saves and settings survive package updates.
Mods: add HD texture packs and Dolphin graphics mods from any folder.
Online play: host a room and share a 4-word room code; no IP addresses needed.

Unlock everything & Local Gecko Codes (Experimental): one switch gives 99,999 tickets and unlocks every cup, machine, Gold Part, Staff Ghost, Story chapter and shop song (works in both Local and Online play), plus 16 optional Gecko codes for Local Play (15 by Ralf, plus the 21:9 ultrawide code) (*Experimental - A work in progress*; automatically disabled in Online rooms).
Windows build: a portable zip for Windows 10/11, with the same launcher and features.
The current target is the game's normal 60 FPS operation. Performance and available AA modes depend on your hardware.
Open CHEATS & UNLOCKS in the launcher and switch on Unlock Everything & Max Tickets (99,999). The unlocks are applied automatically every time the game starts; there are no button codes to enter:
99,999 tickets to spend in the F-Zero Shop.
All cups, including the AX Cup and its tracks.
Every machine, including the AX machines and Dark Schneider.

Every custom part, including the 15 Gold Parts from the hidden shop codes discovered in 2026. They are listed under F-Zero Shop > Custom Parts at 15 tickets each, under their part names: Buy the three parts, then assemble them as a new machine in the Garage.
Sounds of MUTE CITY and Sounds of BIG BLUE for sale under F-Zero Shop > Items (99 tickets). Press Z when choosing a Mute City or Big Blue course to race with the remix; the normal music stays.

A native Windows and Android version of Super Mario All-Stars (SNES) with a launcher, true widescreen, re-anchored HUDs, display options, cheats, level select, achievements, a sound test and a music player. It contains no game data: it runs from your own ROM (Super Mario All-Stars (USA).sfc, CRC32 925637C7); no game starts without it.
Requirements: Windows 10/11, Visual Studio 2022 (C++ workload) and CMake 3.20+. No other libraries are needed (Direct3D 11, Direct2D, XAudio2, XInput and DirectInput come with Windows).
The program is written to build\Release\SuperMarioAllStars.exe.

The same code builds for Android (android/), as the Mickey & Donald Collection's does: SDL2 2.32.10 compiled from source for the window, sound and controllers, OpenGL ES 3.0 for the picture. You need the Android SDK with NDK 28.2 and CMake 3.31.6 (both from the SDK manager) and JDK 17 or later. The SDL2 source belongs in third_party/SDL2-2.32.10-src (android/fetch_sdl.ps1 downloads and checks it), then:

The APK ends up in android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/ (64-bit ARM phones and tablets, Android 6.0 or later, and the x86_64 emulator). Release builds are signed when android/keystore.properties names a keystore (storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias, keyPassword), as the Disney collection's are.

Put the ROM next to the executable, in a roms folder beside it, or in any parent folder up to three levels up; the location is remembered in rompath.txt. Without it the launcher's cards say ROM not found and what is needed, and a ROM copied in while the launcher is open is picked up within a second. Another version or dump of All-Stars runs too, its file name shown in amber on the cards: widescreen, cheats and the level select are tuned for the USA version.
To start a game directly, give SuperMarioAllStars.exe the argument --game smb1, --game smbll, --game smb2 or --game smb3 (for example in a shortcut).

Battery saves go to saves\smas.srm, save states to saves\, screenshots to screenshots\, settings to smas_port.ini. Files are written in full before they replace the old ones, so a full disk can't leave a truncated save (you are told the save failed instead). Save states carry a checksum: a damaged one is refused rather than loaded. They also keep the widescreen state, so a state loads exactly as it was saved, and one saved at a narrower width (or by an older version) brings in the enemies of the wider view. If the graphics driver resets (a driver update or crash), the picture comes back by…

Install the APK (Android asks you to allow installing apps from the place you opened it). On the first start the launcher's card says ROM not found: tap it, pick Super Mario All-Stars (USA).sfc (or a .smc) in the file picker, and it is copied into the app. A ROM can also be put in the app's folder Android/data/com.darhkfox.allstars/files (or a roms folder there) with a computer.

Touch: an SNES pad over the game: the D-pad bottom left, A B X Y bottom right, L and R at the sides, Select and Start bottom centre, Menu top left, and (when they're switched on and achievements are off) rewind and fast forward top right. Tap a game's card to choose it, tap it again to play; in the menus tap a row to use it, drag to scroll, and the button top right goes back.

Controllers and keyboards work as on Windows (the same bindings); the on-screen controls hide while one is in use (*Options → Controls → On-Screen Controls*: While Touching, Always or Never, and their opacity).
Back opens and closes the menu, as Esc does.
The picture fills the screen (*Aspect Ratio: Auto*), with the same filters and colour settings. The window settings, VSync, Black Frame Insertion, High Frame Rate and slang shaders are Windows only.

bloques: A native Windows port of Resident Evil Outbreak (PS2). The game code is statically recompiled from your own disc and runs on a PS2 compatibility runtime, so there is no emulator involved. Both Outbreak File #1 and File #2 are supported, including online co-op.
Download the latest release · Requirements · Report a problem
This is an unofficial fan project. You need your own copy of the game; no game files or game code are included in the download.
File #1, playable start to finish: menus, scenarios, cutscenes, movies, audio and saves.
File #2, with its own import, build and saves.
Online co-op for up to four players. One player hosts from the launcher and the others join by address or on the local network. No accounts or registration.
Graphics options: up to 4× internal resolution, 16:9, 21:9 and 32:9 display modes, FXAA/SMAA, texture filtering, brightness and gamma.
Audio: separate master, music, effects, voice and interface volume, plus optional spoken subtitles.
Controllers: DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox controllers and keyboard, all remappable.
Mods and cheats: a seeded Randomizer for both games, asset replacement packs and built-in cheats. See making mods.
Download RE-Outbreak- -Windows-x64.zip from the latest release, extract it to a new folder and run Outbreak.Launcher.exe. Nothing else needs to be installed.
Click Choose ISO and pick your disc image. Supported discs:

Click Build game. The launcher imports the disc, downloads a compiler and builds the game on your PC. This happens once, needs an internet connection and about 10 GB of free space, and can take an hour or more.

Later launches start straight away. Keep the ISO where it is, since the game reads from it. Your graphics driver needs OpenGL 3.3; Vulkan is used for GPU rendering when available. PAL and Japanese discs are not supported.

Open Co-op and choose Host a game or Join a game. The host shares an address with friends, who either paste it in or pick the game from the local network list. The first time you host, the launcher sets up a small server (it downloads Python if needed); after that it starts immediately.
Over the internet the host has to be reachable. A VPN like Tailscale or ZeroTier is the easiest option. Otherwise forward these ports to the host; the launcher can try to do this for you with UPnP.
Players who join can see the host's IP address. Connections behind carrier-grade NAT usually need a VPN. More detail is in the server setup and networking notes.

Settings, imported discs, builds, memory cards, mods and logs are kept in a data folder next to the launcher, so the whole thing can be moved or backed up as one folder. To keep them somewhere else, use Game files → Storage → Change folder. Updates keep your data.

File #1 and File #2 are both supported on Windows. Some rooms are CPU-heavy, and performance there depends on your processor. A macOS build exists in the source tree (notes) but there is no Mac download yet. Linux support is in progress.

No game data is included. On first start the game asks for your own disc image (ISO, RVZ and or an extracted game folder) of the USA release (GLME01) and/or the European release (GLMP01). It is recommended to use both the USA and PAL versions of the game to experience every feature available in this port. Once the games are selected, it then builds the game for your PC with the bundled compiler, which takes about 20 to 60 seconds on a decent PC.
Any resolution, widescreen and ultrawide: Hor+, with HUD elements anchored to the screen edges and widescreen fixes for full-screen scenes.

High frame rates: game logic stays at the original 30 updates per second, and the frames in between are interpolated from source-tagged objects. Frame rate goes up to 320 fps, with "Match display refresh rate" and VRR/G-SYNC aware pacing. "Original" keeps the console's 30 fps.

Accurate GameCube rendering: Better than Dolphin. EFB copies including copy-to-RAM, depth textures, real-time shadows, indirect effects, 6-bit blending and copy filters. A shader precache prepares everything before the game starts, so there are no compile stutters.
Optional Enhanced lighting: per-pixel and colored lights, soft shadows, a realistic flashlight beam, bloom and ghosts cast a glowing light.
The European Hidden Mansion, including its boss changes. With both discs, E. Gadd's lab offers the USA and the European Hidden Mansion.
Restored unused content, all off by default: Toggles to re-enable various cut content, a model viewer, warps to unused rooms and more.
Options for EVERYTHING: an F1 options menu for everything, difficulty settings, fun tweaks and toggles, rendering options, etc
The 2-player mode (Unused content) is unfinished. The plan is to finish it soon, but for now it's mostly in the state it was left in in the original code.
[!NOTE] A special thank you to Thomu, Moro, and JMOTZU for their extensive playtesting in the Co-op mod. Also, a special thank you to Thomu for his generous support towards the project's development.
Fan-subtitled Japanese FMVs: one optional Japanese FMVs mod with a subtitle dropdown from acediez/Hondoori (English) and El Retro Dan (Spanish), with full attribution and preserved upstream readmes.
Mega Man X4 on Windows and Linux. 1.0.27 Stable Public Beta, with two-player co-op. Bring a friend through X's or Zero's campaign, on one computer or over netplay.
Downloads · What's new in 1.0.27 · Known issues

Play X and Zero simultaneously, with their own attacks, voices and effects. Player 1 owns the story, boss clears and permanent progress; Player 2 joins as the other hero. Arrive together, tackle bosses together, and share team retries. The hero who lands a boss's final hit gets their victory theme.
The extra boss encounters, scaling and character codes are off by default. The netplay host chooses the shared options.
One shared world, two independent netplay views.
Double and Iris in one co-op run, when you enable the option.
Download the Windows x64 ZIP and extract it, or use the Linux x86_64 AppImage (glibc 2.38 or newer).
Select your own original, unmodified Mega Man X4 USA (SLUS-00561) disc image. Choose the .cue from a .cue + .bin set. OpenBIOS is included; a separate BIOS dump is optional.

For local co-op, enable Mods → X + Zero Co-op, assign Player 1 and Player 2 in Controls, and choose Local co-op display for Unified or side by side 8:3, then press Play. For netplay, press Netplay and host or join using X + Zero Co-op. Both peers need the same release.

Only the verified original USA disc is accepted, including when every mod is disabled. All changes belong in Mods. Patched discs, undubs and retranslated disc images are unsupported; use the corresponding mods over the original disc.
Co-op requires OpenGL and takes effect on a fresh game boot. Single-player remains available.

With side by side 8:3 or Split netplay, each player sees their own character's weapon or technique award, including its artwork and instructions. P1 advances the shared award and Save/Continue flow; both heroes share the campaign's unlocks. Unified uses P1's award screen.

Fast loading is built in. The old CD Speed and Fast Loading mods are retired; the game now keeps verified disc data in memory and feeds it through the original loading routines. Music and cutscenes retain their normal timing.

Offline co-op also supports save states (F7) and rewind (F8) when enabled. The Mods page includes widescreen, character codes and optional input display and diagnostic recording, off by default. Controls, saves and reporting guide →

Optional language mods offer Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese dialogue using the game's own font. Supply your Japanese Rockman X4 disc to choose Japanese movies, voices and the title screen independently. Translations are drafts awaiting native-speaker review. Language setup and scope →

Complete Story is an optional local solo/co-op mod, off by default. Add Zero's playable Memorial Hall duel, fight both Double and Iris, and watch the additional Colonel, Iris and Zero/Sigma movies in your campaign. Complete Story setup and scope →
Expect bugs; independent cameras can still slow down. Online sign-in/startup reports remain under investigation. Check the burndown or report a bug.
Nookery (formerly known as ACGC-PC-Port) is a native Windows/Linux/macOS/Android/iOS port of Animal Crossing (GameCube), based on the ac-decomp decompilation.
This repository contains no game assets. A legally obtained GAFE01 Rev 0 (USA) disc image is required. RVZ, ISO, CISO and GCM images are supported.
Download the latest release in the Releases page.
Optionally download the texture pack (Highly recommended, made by extremely talented artists, it looks really good.) and put the extracted files under {your_data_folder}/texture_pack
Run Nookery. You'll need to select your legally obtained Animal Crossing copy to play the game.

Nookery includes various toggleable quality of life changes, we recommend taking a look under gameplay tab in settings. You might also want to take a peek at features to have an idea about what to expect.
If you have a save you want to import, you can drop them under {your_data_folder}/saves/card_a. You can also use card_b for the towns you want to visit.
If you are having issues with your controller/Steam Deck acting weird with inputs, try closing steam, or adding Nookery as a non-steam game.
On iOS, see INSTALLING_IOS.md to install the .ipa with iloader.
See BUILDING.md for Windows, Linux, and macOS, BUILDING_ANDROID.md for Android, and BUILDING_IOS.md for iOS. You can use Nookery --help to see available command line options after building.
The data folder holds saves, config.json, input.json, texture_pack/, and nes_roms/. Its default location is:
For android, you might need to use a different file browser app such as Material Files if you can't see internal files of Nookery.
On desktop, use Settings > Data to move game data to a custom folder.
Your main town is at save/card_a/ in the data folder. We support .gci files, you can just use your dolphin save if you are migrating. You can put multiple towns in save/card_b/ to visit them in game.
Native 64-bit Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS support, with Vulkan, D3D12, D3D11 and Metal renderers via Aurora
Full mouse support for walking, inventory and all of the overlays
Controller support with hotplug, button remapping and stick deadzones
Touch controls on Android/iOS, with a layout editor and vibration
Built-in NES emulator that allows loading your own ROMs from the nes_roms folder
Multiple towns in Card B so you can select where you want to visit easily
Ability to visit the island without a GBA
Extended date support up to year 3000
Quality-of-life options: fast text, single-player shop upgrades, optional Resetti, outdoor camera control, tool switch with D-pad and more!

He gave me access to deluxe's code even though he had no reason to (the reason this port got so much QoL from deluxe mod!), and was always helpful whenever I had questions about how the game worked. It was a lot of fun working together, thanks man.

Also special thanks to Encounter for handling so much of the Aurora migration and their massive help, Tom Lube for extensive private testing, Aurora developers, Dusklight team for both their help and advice, and all contributors. This project couldn't get where it is without you.

Final Fantasy Tactics Advance, running natively on your Windows PC, Linux PC, Steam Deck or Android. Widescreen, video and audio options, and a one-click installer.

FFTARecomp turns Final Fantasy Tactics Advance into a native program for Windows, Linux, Steam Deck and Android. Instead of running in an emulator, the game is recompiled from your own ROM, so it runs smoothly, needs no BIOS, and gets modern options. It is based on gba-recomp by JRickey.
🕹️ Steam Deck: the port menu now opens with Y.
📱 Much better mouse and touch support on Android. Most of the game is now playable with this mode.
📜 Scrollbars were added so menus are more comfortable to use with the mouse and touch.
The game now creates an auto save every 5 seconds, so you can close the game at any time, anywhere, without losing progress.
The slot limit of the base game was raised: you can now have more than 2 save slots.
⏩ New x1.5 speed for fast forward.
🖥️ Menus redesigned for widescreen, without black borders, repeating the gradient patterns of the game's own textures.

Please keep in mind that the menu background is just an image, and stretching the render area doesn't magically extend everything in the menu. This is my best effort to widen it; a better option would be to recreate the artwork from scratch, but I don't have much artistic experience.
🔍 Smooth zoom: zooming in and out is now animated instead of instant, and some UI elements that didn't scale with zoom out now do.
💬 Visual bugs fixed related to text bubbles.
🎞️ Visual bugs fixed related to the enter and exit animations of the menus, plus other visual fixes.
🤖 Native Android version, with touch support that works like the PC mouse support. To enable it, go to Input > Touchscreen > Touch Controls.

🖱️ Mouse support: it doesn't cover the whole game yet, but support keeps expanding. To enable it, go to Input > Mouse and Keyboard and turn it on. On Windows, mouse mode comes with its own remappable layout that doesn't affect the keyboard controls.
⚡ Lightweight install: the install size is only about 11 MB (it used to be roughly 800 MB), and compile time is about 4 seconds (it used to be roughly 120 seconds).
💬 Fully reworked game UI and editable text bubbles: the Text Bubbles option in the Settings menu lets you adjust their length and size in-game.
🇪🇺 European ROM support. Saves are compatible between regions.
🎨 Video options: screen model, grid, scaling and vsync.
🔊 Normal audio mode: the game fast-forwards while the audio keeps playing at normal speed.
🕹️ Steam Deck support, with a dedicated installer (the Linux installer also works).
🛠️ Reworked installer and a one-click installer: pick your ROM and you're done.
💡 To open the Options Menu, press Esc while in-game.
Controls can be remapped from the Options Menu.
Download FFTARecomp-windows-x86_64.zip from Releases and extract it.
Run FFTARecomp.exe, choose your ROM and press Recompile & Install.
Wait for the five steps to finish, then press Play. ▶️
Download FFTARecomp-linux-x86_64.tar.gz from Releases and run:
On Steam Deck, run it from Desktop Mode.
Tap the downloaded file and press Install. If Android asks, allow installing apps from this source.
Open the app and choose your ROM.
💡 You need your own copy of Final Fantasy Tactics Advance. This project does not include any game data.
A fan mod of Dino Crisis (PS1, 1999): the game is rebuilt from your own disc into a native Windows program, made to look and play like the Resident Evil remakes.
Download: DinoCrisisME_Setup.exe on the Releases page.
Choose the folder where to install and press Install.
Remove the game: Uninstall.exe in its folder.
Without the setup window: download DinoCrisisME_unpacked.zip from Releases (the same files Setup carries), unpack it and run from that folder:
Graphics improvements: shadows, ambient occlusion, anti-aliasing and more
Widescreen 16:9, 21:9 and 32:9 without stretching, or the original 4:3
Render resolution up to 4K, 30 to 1000 FPS
Keyboard and mouse or a gamepad, every button can be remapped
Mod support: a mods folder the game picks up while running, and Dino Crisis ME Studio to export and replace characters, rooms, textures, sounds and videos

Nothing of the game is in this repository or in the installer. Setup reads your own disc image, recompiles the game's code to C and builds it on your PC together with the mod (a few minutes). The compiler and everything else it needs come with Setup.
That is also why there is no ready-made game to download: the built game contains code from your disc.
Your own Dino Crisis disc image (Track 1 .bin or .cue), one of:
.sbi is the LibCrypt file of a PAL disc, next to the image (the same file DuckStation uses).
Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, a graphics card with Vulkan.
Integrated graphics. At the first start the game turns its graphics down once: Shadows off, Ambient Occlusion Low, Anti-Aliasing SMAA. You can change them in Modern Options > Graphics.

Windows 11 Smart App Control. If setup stops at "Recompiling the game to C", this Windows feature is probably on. It only lets through apps it already knows, and the game is built from your disc right on your PC, so to Windows it is a brand-new app. To install and play, set Smart App Control to Off (Windows Security > App & browser control > Smart App Control settings) and run setup again.

Send the log to the developer: DinoCrisisME_log.txt next to DinoCrisisME.exe, or install-log.txt in the install folder if setup stopped. Attach it to an issue, or use the Discord link in the game's main menu.
mod/ - everything Setup uses to build the game:
src/ - the mod's runtime: renderer, camera, controls, menus, BIOS replacement, mods loader
patches/ - the mod's changes to the recompiler framework
generated/, versions/ - hooks into the recompiled game code, per disc version
shaders/, assets/, config/, collision/ - shaders, the mod's own images and data, default settings, camera collision
build/, project/, tools/ - build plans, the game project, the scripts Setup runs
installer/ - the setup window (Setup.cs), the install script (dcme_install.py), the uninstaller, the README that comes with Setup
Not here: the compiler (llvm-mingw), Python, SDL2 and the Vulkan headers. Setup and DinoCrisisME_unpacked.zip carry them. The recompiler framework psxrecomp is downloaded by Setup at a fixed commit.
The mod's own files: MIT (LICENSE). Recompiler framework and the mod's changes to it: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Other parts: mod/THIRD-PARTY.txt.
Dino Crisis belongs to Capcom. This is a free fan mod, not made or endorsed by Capcom. The installed game holds code recompiled from your disc: for your own use, do not share or sell it.
Rediscover Hoenn. Two screens. A new perspective. A native Nintendo 3DS port with a touch interface and an optional voxel overworld.
Get the latest version — directly in your browser
Visit emerald-3ds.com to generate and download the latest version from your own supported ROM. No desktop builder or source code download is required.

The website includes the complete installation and update instructions, sound setup and frequently asked questions. Start there whether you are installing for the first time, updating or troubleshooting.

Need help? Please read the instructions and FAQ on emerald-3ds.com before opening an issue or asking on Discord. If your question is still unanswered, include your console or emulator, game version and the exact error message when asking for help.
Screenshots · Features · Web builder, instructions & FAQ · Documentation · Community · Support the project

Emerald 3DS brings the adventure to Nintendo 3DS as native homebrew. The game runs on the top screen, while a dedicated touch interface on the bottom screen replaces the START menu. Enable the optional voxel overworld to explore supported areas from a new angle.
A look at the adventure across both screens.

The voxel overworld is off by default. Open OPTION on the bottom screen and enable VOXEL 3D, then adjust 3D ANGLE and 3D ZOOM to set your camera. On a New 3DS, raise the 3D slider for a stereoscopic world; 3D WORLD and 3D DEPTH (OPTION → SETTINGS, second page) control it.

3D mode is a work in progress. Many towns and routes now have modelled buildings and relief, but large parts of the map and most interiors are still shown flat, and the Battle Frontier is only an early start. More areas will be modelled as the project moves forward.

In OPTION → ENHANCEMENTS, set DAY / NIGHT to AUTO to enable outdoor lighting inspired by HeartGold/SoulSilver. It is OFF by default; indoors, caves, underwater areas, menus and classic battles keep their original colours. Nights have a soft moonlit blue, and supported voxel windows and street lamps glow warm.

CLOCK SPEED selects 1X, 6X, 12X, 24X, 60X or 120X. At 1X, lighting follows Emerald's own clock; higher speeds advance a separate clock (60X is a day in 24 real minutes) and berries grow with it. Daily events and the GBA save format stay original, and time with the console asleep or off runs at 1X. Back up emerald3ds.clock and emerald3ds.clock.bak together with emerald3ds.sav.

WILD POKEMON → TIMED changes some grass encounters by morning, day and night on routes 101–104, 110, 116–117, 119–121 and 123 (ORIGINAL, the default, keeps the original tables). SHOW CLOCK → ON adds the time to the bottom screen's map. More in the day/night guide.

OPTION → ENHANCEMENTS → FOLLOWER makes your lead Pokémon walk behind you. Its sprites and messages come from HeartGold/SoulSilver: the builder downloads them while it builds (the only step that needs an Internet connection; without one, the game is built without them).

Local wireless play is experimental: two to four consoles with the same version and language can meet in the Union Room and use the link features of Pokémon Centers, the Berry Blender, contests and the Battle Tower. Expect bugs, and back up your save before trying it.
Open emerald-3ds.com and follow the instructions for your console or emulator.
Select your own clean, supported Pokémon Emerald ROM in the web builder (see supported cartridges).
Generate and download the game files, then follow the website's installation guide to place them correctly.
Complete the sound setup described in the guide before launching the game.

bloques: Ship of Harkinian — Android, iOS, and tvOS
Linkzenic's Android, iOS, and Apple TV ports of Harbour Masters' Ship of Harkinian, together in one repository.
This repository now focuses on standard Ship of Harkinian. NEI, Cel Shading, and Fusion are not included in the unified release.
The repository was renamed from Shipwright-Android to Shipwright-Ports. Existing GitHub links redirect here.
Download published builds from Releases. Read the notes for the release you install; the latest published release may not yet include every platform.
The unified Android, iOS, and tvOS release is available: 9.3.1 Ports Release. GitHub Actions artifacts are build candidates, not published releases.
No game ROMs or extracted game assets are included. You must supply a supported, legally obtained Ocarina of Time ROM. Check compatibility with the ROM checker or supported hashes.
Customizable Classic, N64, GameCube, and Modern touch layouts.
A layout editor with movable, resizable, and individually hideable controls.
Independent touch assignments, manual-jump options, extra item buttons, modifier assignments, and floating-stick controls.
Item icons, contextual actions, Fairy, and Map controls integrated into the touch layouts.
Download the standard Android APK from Releases.
Install it over your existing Linkzenic standard SOH app to retain its app data. Do not uninstall first.
On first setup, choose the user-data folder and allow the app to prepare its support files.
Select your supported ROM when prompted to extract game data.
Android requires Android 7 or later and compatible OpenGL ES 3.0 hardware. Standard SOH uses the selected SOH user-data folder; check Settings > General for the active location.

Use the Android back gesture/button or the mapped controller menu button to open settings. Physical-controller mappings are under Settings > Controls; touch options are under Settings > Touch Controls.
Customizable Classic, N64, GameCube, and Modern touch layouts.
A layout editor with movable, resizable, and individually hideable controls.
Independent touch assignments, manual-jump options, extra item buttons, modifier assignments, and floating-stick controls.

Apple downloads are unsigned IPAs unless a release explicitly says otherwise. Sign and install them using a compatible signing method. Keep the same app identifier and signing setup when updating; do not delete the existing app if you want to retain its local data.

Use the app's file-import options to add compatible game data generated from your own supported ROM. Local files remain available offline. On correctly provisioned builds, the app automatically creates the visible SOH folder in iCloud Drive. A folder-picker fallback is available when native iCloud Documents access is unavailable.

Sync checks run while the app is active and at launch/foreground. External settings and resource changes apply after restarting. Deletions do not automatically propagate. Runtime logs, caches, temporary files, and sync bookkeeping are excluded.
